criteria.criterion: with a model-class table configured to values that DIFFER from cfg.model, no hand-built SUB-CALL in review-plan, review-code or verify-completion resolves to cfg.model — verified IN-SESSION by tests/unit/test_subcall_class_selection.py

each of the THREE hand-built sub-call sites selects its model from the class vocabulary, and the class chosen for each is stated in the code with its reason: enrich.py (ticket-digest) -> trivial, overlap/judge.py (overlap-judge) -> standard, code_review/workflow_ops.py::score_code_novelty (code-novelty) -> standard. operations.py::review_ticket is DELIBERATELY left on cfg.model and registered in _CFG_MODEL_BY_DESIGN

code-novelty's choice is consistent with plan-review's novelty sub-call, or the difference is documented as deliberate at both sites — score_code_novelty's docstring currently claims it 'mirrors' _score_floor_novelty, which uses _verifier_cfg, and that parity does not hold

a test fails if ANY hand-built sub-call inherits cfg.model while a class table is configured — the general defect, so a future hand-built sub-call cannot silently reintroduce it. A test that enumerates today's four sites by name does NOT satisfy this

the overlap-judge test constructs its trigger deliberately: wire.py:overlap_findings runs the judge only when BM25F retrieval returns candidates, so a test that merely runs a gate and hopes the judge fires will silently pass while testing nothing
ticket-digest's fix holds on the STORE WRITE path, not only inside a gate run
fail-safe behaviour is preserved at every site: the novelty signal must still degrade to 'keep more findings', and the overlap step must remain advisory and never block a review
